mainTopic: Written and oral תורה, and the משנה's rules of דרכי שלום: the עירוב, sharing river water, and traps
overview: This עמוד opens by finishing a list of תורה sections tied to the service in the משכן. Then רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן argue whether most of the תורה was given in writing or by word of mouth, and each explains away the other's פסוק. Next come teachings that the written תורה must stay written and the oral תורה must stay oral, and that the ברית with Israel was made for the sake of the oral תורה. The גמרא then returns to the משנה's rules of דרכי שלום. An עירוב stays in its usual house to avoid suspicion against the owner, not for his honor. רב and שמואל argue whether the lower or upper fields along a river water first when the river must be dammed, and since no הלכה was decided, כל דאלים גבר. Two stories about אביי and river water follow. The עמוד ends by starting the משנה's rule about animals caught in another person's trap, which continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Finishing the list of sections tied to the משכן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a list of תורה sections connected to the service in the משכן: the section of כהנים who drank wine, the section of the lamps, and the section of the פרה אדומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the section about those who drank wine, and the section of the lamps, and the section of the פרה אדומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a list it began before this piece. These are the last three sections in it, all connected to the service in the משכן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line is the tail end of the earlier discussion, not a new idea. These three sections are listed because each was needed for the service in the משכן: כהנים may not serve after drinking wine, the lamps had to be lit, and the פרה אדומה was needed for purity.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who drank wine (כהנים who may not serve while drunk)
The red heifer, used for purifying from טומאת מת

phrases.english: and the section of those who drank wine,
phrases.notes: This is the part about כהנים who drank wine and can't do the עבודה, in ויקרא 10:8–11.

phrases.english: and the section of the lamps,
and the section of the red heifer.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפָרָשַׁת שְׁתוּיֵי יַיִן, וּפָרָשַׁת נֵרוֹת, וּפָרָשַׁת פָּרָה אֲדוּמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a list from the previous section of the דף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These three sections complete the list of sections tied to the service in the משכן.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: Most of the תורה is written
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says the larger part of the תורה was given in writing and the smaller part orally. His proof is the פסוק in הושע, 'I wrote for him the greater part of My תורה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: The תורה is mostly written and a minority oral, as it says: 'I wrote for him the greater part of My תורה; they were considered like a stranger.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבי אלעזר says most of the תורה was given in writing, and he proves it from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר reads the פסוק as a plain statement: 'I wrote' the 'greater part' (רובי) of My תורה. So the written part is the majority.

keyTerms.meaning: The greater part of My תורה

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
The Torah – the majority is in writing
and a minority is oral,
as it is stated: “I wrote for him the greater part of My Torah;
phrases.notes: הושע 8:12

phrases.english: they were considered like a stranger.”

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: תּוֹרָה – רוֹב בִּכְתָב וּמִיעוּט עַל פֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the written and oral תורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Most of the תורה is written; the minority is oral.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: Most of the תורה is oral
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees. He says the larger part of the תורה is oral and the smaller part written. His proof is the פסוק 'כי על פי הדברים האלה', where 'על פי' hints at 'by mouth.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: Mostly oral and a minority written, as it says: 'For על פי (by the mouth of) these words.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן argues with רבי אלעזר. He says most of the תורה is oral, and he brings his own פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן reads the words על פי ('by the mouth of') as pointing to the oral תורה. The ברית was made on the basis of the oral teachings, which shows they are the main part. Now there are two opposite views, each with a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'by the mouth of'; read here as a hint to the oral תורה

steps.confusionAlert: Both אמוראים agree there is a written תורה and an oral תורה. They only argue about which part is bigger.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
The majority is oral and a minority is in writing,
as it is stated: “For on the basis of these matters.”
phrases.notes: שמות 34:27. He hears על פי as 'by mouth,' so the ברית rests mainly on what is taught orally.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: רוֹב עַל פֶּה וּמִיעוּט בִּכְתָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite view to רבי אלעזר's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Most of the תורה is oral; the minority is written.

steps.title: How does רבי יוחנן explain רבי אלעזר's פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן: the פסוק in הושע says plainly 'I wrote for him the greater part of My תורה'. How can he say most is oral?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one too: isn't it written, 'I wrote for him the greater part of My תורה'?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks רבי יוחנן how he deals with the פסוק that seems to say most of the תורה is written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's own פסוק doesn't cancel רבי אלעזר's פסוק. The words 'I wrote the greater part' seem to go straight against רבי יוחנן, so he must explain them.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the other אמורא)

phrases.english: And the other one too, isn't it written:
phrases.notes: 'The other one' here is רבי יוחנן. How does he handle רבי אלעזר's פסוק?

phrases.english: “I wrote for him the greater part of My Torah”!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ נָמֵי, הָכְתִיב: אֶכְתּוֹב לוֹ רוּבֵּי תּוֹרָתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן with רבי אלעזר's פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that most of the תורה is oral
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plain meaning of the פסוק in הושע is that the greater part of the תורה was written.

steps.title: The פסוק is an amazed question
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reads the פסוק as a question of amazement: 'Should I write the greater part of My תורה for him? Then they would be considered like strangers!'
steps.simpleTranslation: That פסוק is said in amazement: Shall I write for him the greater part of My תורה?! Then they would be considered like a stranger!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי יוחנן. The פסוק is not a statement but a question of surprise, which actually supports his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read as a question, the פסוק means: if I had written most of the תורה, Israel would be like strangers, no different from the nations. So most of the תורה must stay oral. The same פסוק that seemed to go against רבי יוחנן now helps him.

keyTerms.meaning: He is saying it in amazement (as a surprised question)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common tool of the גמרא: the same Hebrew words can be read as a statement or as a question, and that can flip the meaning.

phrases.english: That one, it is said in amazement:
Shall I write for him the greater part of My Torah?!
Then wouldn't “they be considered like a stranger”!
phrases.notes: If everything were written, Israel would have nothing special over the other nations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the פסוק as a rhetorical question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק states as a fact that most of the תורה was written.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק asks in amazement whether most should be written, and answers no: then Israel would be like strangers.

steps.title: How does רבי אלעזר explain רבי יוחנן's פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: Now the גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר: the פסוק says the ברית was made 'על פי', on the basis of the oral words. Doesn't that show the oral part is the main part?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one too: isn't it written, 'For על פי these words'?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבי אלעזר and asks how he deals with רבי יוחנן's פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This mirrors the challenge in step 4. If the ברית is based on the oral teachings, it seems the oral part is the bigger one, which goes against רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: And the other one too, isn't it written:
phrases.notes: Now 'the other one' is רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: “For on the basis of these matters”!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ נָמֵי, הָכְתִיב: כִּי עַל פִּי הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 4, this time against רבי אלעזר.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's view that most of the תורה is written
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק makes the ברית depend on the oral words, which suggests they are the main and larger part.

steps.title: The oral part is stressed because it is harder to learn
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers that the פסוק stresses the oral תורה because it is harder to learn, not because it is the bigger part.
steps.simpleTranslation: That פסוק is because they are difficult to learn.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי אלעזר: the פסוק puts weight on the oral teachings because they are harder to master.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is about importance and difficulty, not size. Oral teachings are harder to learn and hold onto, so the ברית is tied to them. That still fits רבי אלעזר's view that the written part is bigger.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר: most of the תורה is written (from 'אכתוב לו רובי תורתי'). רבי יוחנן: most is oral (from 'על פי הדברים האלה'). רבי יוחנן reads הושע as an amazed question. רבי אלעזר says על פי stresses the oral part only because it is harder to learn.

phrases.english: That one – it is because they are difficult to learn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רבי אלעזר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the reason for the פסוק's emphasis
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברית rests on the oral words because they are the majority.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברית is tied to the oral words because they are harder to learn, not because there are more of them.

steps.title: Written words stay written, oral words stay oral
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בר נחמני points out that one פסוק says both 'write' and 'by mouth.' He resolves it: the written תורה may not be said by heart, and the oral תורה may not be written down.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בר נחמני, the speaker for ריש לקיש, taught: One part of the פסוק says 'Write for yourself these words,' and another part says 'by the mouth of these words.' How do these fit together? Words that were given in writing, you may not say by heart. Words that were given orally, you may not put in writing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה בר נחמני notices two phrases in the same פסוק that seem to pull in opposite directions, 'write' and 'by mouth.' He settles it by giving each kind of תורה its own rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'כתוב לך' tells us the written תורה must stay in writing. The phrase 'על פי' tells us the oral תורה must stay oral. So each kind of תורה keeps its own form, and you may not switch one into the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught a lesson drawn from a פסוק
The speaker who repeated a rabbi's teaching out loud to the crowd
How can this be? (used when two sources seem to clash)
Given orally, by mouth (the oral תורה)

steps.confusionAlert: Both quotes come from the same פסוק (שמות 34:27). They are not two different פסוקים. The 'clash' is between two phrases inside one פסוק.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda bar Naḥmani expounded,
the speaker for Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish,
It is written: "Write for yourself these words,"
phrases.notes: שמות 34:27

phrases.english: and it is written: "For by the mouth of these words" —
phrases.notes: Same פסוק, a few words later. 'על פי' literally means 'by the mouth of.'

phrases.english: How can this be?

phrases.aramaic: דְּבָרִים שֶׁבִּכְתָב אִי אַתָּה רַשַּׁאי לְאוֹמְרָן עַל פֶּה,
phrases.english: Words that are written, you may not say them by heart;

phrases.aramaic: דְּבָרִים שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה אִי אַתָּה רַשַּׁאי לְאוֹמְרָן בִּכְתָב,
phrases.english: words that are oral, you may not say them in writing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same פסוק ('על פי הדברים האלה') that came up in steps 3 to 7, but now draws a new rule from it: each kind of תורה must keep its own form.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The written תורה may not be recited by heart, and the oral תורה may not be written down.

steps.title: The school of רבי ישמעאל: write these, not הלכות
steps.stepSummary: A teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל reads the word 'אלה' (these) as limiting: only these words may be written, not the הלכות of the oral תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: The word 'these' means only these you may write. You may not write הלכות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל that reaches the same rule from a different word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the lesson comes from the word 'אלה.' It means 'these and nothing else': write only the words of the written תורה. The הלכות of the oral תורה are left out, so they may not be written.

keyTerms.meaning: The study house (school) of רבי ישמעאל

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"These": these you write,
phrases.notes: The word 'אלה' in 'כתוב לך את הדברים האלה' is read as 'only these.'

phrases.english: but you do not write הלכות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up step 8's rule that the oral תורה may not be written, using the word 'אלה' as the source instead.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the written תורה may be written; הלכות of the oral תורה may not be written.

steps.title: The ברית was made for the sake of the oral תורה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says הקדוש ברוך הוא made His ברית with Israel only because of the oral תורה, based on 'על פי הדברים האלה כרתי אתך ברית.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: הקדוש ברוך הוא made a ברית with Israel only for the sake of the oral words, as it says: 'For by the mouth of these words I have made a ברית with you and with Israel.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן brings the end of the same פסוק to show how important the oral תורה is. The ברית was made because of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links the ברית to 'על פי' ('by the mouth of') these words. רבי יוחנן reads that as the oral תורה, so the ברית depends on the oral תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy One, Blessed be He
For the sake of, because of

steps.whatToRemember: The oral תורה must stay oral and the written תורה must stay written. The ברית with Israel is tied to the oral תורה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא כָּרַת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּרִית עִם יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, did not make a covenant with Israel
except for the sake of the oral words,
as it is stated: "For by the mouth of these words
phrases.notes: שמות 34:27

phrases.english: I have made a covenant with you and with Israel."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the oral and written תורה discussion by showing how central the oral תורה is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברית between הקדוש ברוך הוא and Israel was made for the sake of the oral תורה.

steps.title: Why keep the עירוב in the old house?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's rule that an עירוב is placed in the old house מפני דרכי שלום, and asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: We place the עירוב in the old house, because of the ways of peace. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. It asks why keeping the עירוב in its usual house brings peace. This sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says only 'מפני דרכי שלום' without explaining how. The גמרא wants to know what kind of trouble would happen if the עירוב were moved.

keyTerms.meaning: Shared food that joins neighbors' courtyards so they may carry on שבת
The old house, where the עירוב was always kept
The ways of peace (a rule made to keep peace between people)

phrases.english: We place the eiruv in the old house,
because of the ways of peace.
What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְעָרְבִין בְּבַיִת יָשָׁן מִפְּנֵי דַּרְכֵי שָׁלוֹם מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: the גמרא leaves the oral תורה discussion and returns to explain the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly is the peace-related reason for keeping the עירוב in the old house?

steps.title: Not for honor: the charity box moved from house to house
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the reason is honor for the homeowner, then rejects it. A charity box was moved from רב יהודה to רבה to רב יוסף to אביי to רבא, so moving such things is no insult.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is because of honor, there is a problem. A certain charity box was first in רב יהודה's house, then in רבה's house, then in רב יוסף's house, then in אביי's house, then in רבא's house!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one possible reason, honor for the person in whose house the עירוב was kept, and knocks it down right away with a story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If moving a community item insulted the old homeowner, great rabbis would not have kept moving the charity box from house to house. Since they did, moving such an item is not an insult, so honor cannot be the reason.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (offers a possible answer that will be rejected)

phrases.english: If we say it is because of honor,
phrases.notes: He means honor for the owner of the house where the עירוב was always kept.

phrases.english: but there was that charity box,
phrases.notes: Literally 'שופר'; here it's a box for collecting charity.

phrases.english: which was at first in Rav Yehuda's house,
and afterward in Rabba's house,
and afterward in Rav Yosef's house,
and afterward in Abaye's house,
and afterward in Rava's house!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא מִשּׁוּם כָּבוֹד וְהָא הָהוּא שִׁיפּוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to step 11's question and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the עירוב stays in the old house out of honor for the homeowner
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Community items like the charity box were moved from one rabbi's house to another without concern for honor, so honor cannot explain the rule.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects 'honor' as the reason behind the משנה's rule
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Moving a community item from someone's house is not treated as an insult, as the charity box story shows.

steps.title: The real reason: to avoid suspicion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes the reason is חשדא: if the עירוב were moved, people might suspect the old homeowner of wrongdoing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is because of suspicion.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting 'honor,' the גמרא gives the real reason: moving the עירוב could make people suspect the old homeowner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The charity box was moved openly and as a normal thing. An עירוב that suddenly leaves its usual house could make people think the neighbors no longer trust the owner, for example that he took from the food. Keeping it in place prevents this bad talk and protects the peace.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (brings the correct answer after a rejected one)

steps.whatToRemember: The עירוב stays in its usual house so that the owner is not suspected of wrongdoing (חשדא), not because of his honor.

phrases.english: Rather, it is because of suspicion.
phrases.notes: If the עירוב were moved, people might think the neighbors suspect the old homeowner of something.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected 'honor' reason from step 12 with the accepted reason.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The עירוב stays in the old house to avoid suspicion against the homeowner.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: דרכי שלום here means preventing suspicion that moving the עירוב would cause.

steps.title: Who waters first along a river: lower fields or upper fields
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the pit near the irrigation channel, then brings a מחלוקת: רב says the lower fields water first, and שמואל says the upper fields water first.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says a pit near the channel is filled first. It was taught: about people who live along a river, רב says the people at the bottom water first, and שמואל says the people at the top water first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and brings an argument between רב and שמואל about sharing river water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Several people have fields along one river and all want water for their fields. רב gives first rights to the lower (downstream) fields. שמואל gives first rights to the upper (upstream) fields. The גמרא will soon explain exactly when they argue and why.

keyTerms.meaning: An irrigation channel that carries water to fields or pits
People whose fields are along a river
The lower ones (downstream) / the upper ones (upstream)

phrases.english: A pit that is near the irrigation channel, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the opening words of the משנה line being discussed now: that pit gets filled first.

phrases.english: It was stated: people along a river;

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָמַר: תַּתָּאֵי שָׁתוּ מַיָּא בְּרֵישָׁא,
phrases.english: Rav said: the lower ones drink the water first,
phrases.notes: "Drink the water" here means watering their fields.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אֲמַר: עִילָּאֵי שָׁתוּ מַיָּא בְּרֵישָׁא.
phrases.english: and Shmuel said: the upper ones drink the water first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the עירוב clause of the משנה (steps 11-13) to the next clause, about the pit near the channel.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: downstream fields water first. שמואל: upstream fields water first.

steps.title: When they argue: only when the river must be dammed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits the מחלוקת. When water flows on its own, all agree. They argue only when someone must dam the river to water his field. שמואל's upper owners say 'we are closer'; רב's lower owners say 'let the river flow its natural way.'
steps.simpleTranslation: When the water just flows, everyone agrees. They argue about damming the river to water fields. שמואל says the upper ones go first, because they say 'we are closer.' רב says the lower ones go first, because they say 'let the river run its normal course.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly what case רב and שמואל argue about, and gives the reason for each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If water reaches each field by itself, there is nothing to argue about. The fight starts when watering means blocking the river, which keeps water from the people below. The upper owners claim priority because they are nearer to the source. The lower owners say nobody may block the river's natural flow until they have taken what they need.

keyTerms.meaning: When the water flows on its own
To dam the river and water the fields

phrases.english: Where it flows, everyone agrees.
phrases.notes: When the water reaches each field by itself, anyone may water whenever he wants.

phrases.english: When they disagree, it is about damming and watering;

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: עִילָּאֵי שָׁתוּ מַיָּא בְּרֵישָׁא,
phrases.english: Shmuel said: the upper ones drink the water first,
because they say: we are closer.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב אָמַר: תַּתָּאֵי שָׁתוּ מַיָּא בְּרֵישָׁא,
phrases.english: And Rav said: the lower ones drink the water first,
because they say: let the river go its natural way.
phrases.notes: The lower owners mean: let it flow down to us first, and after that you can dam it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the exact case and the reasoning behind the מחלוקת in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מחלוקת is only about damming. שמואל favors the upstream owners because they are closer; רב favors the downstream owners because the river's natural flow comes first.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב and שמואל argue about all river water. They argue only when the river has to be dammed; when the water flows by itself, all agree.

steps.title: The משנה seems to favor whoever is closest, against רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב from the משנה: the pit closest to the channel is filled first. That sounds like 'closer goes first,' which is שמואל's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: the pit near the channel is filled first, because of the ways of peace. That seems to go against רב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב's view using the words of our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives first rights to the pit nearest the water source. That matches שמואל's reasoning, 'we are closer.' So it seems to be a problem for רב, who says the lower ones, farther along the flow, go first.

keyTerms.meaning: Ways of peace: a rule made to prevent fights

phrases.english: We learned: the pit that is near the channel,
is filled first, because of the ways of peace!
phrases.notes: The exclamation point means: this looks like שמואל's 'closer goes first' and is hard for רב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רב's view from step 15 against the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that the downstream owners water first
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה gives priority to whoever is nearest the water, which matches שמואל's 'we are closer' and seems to contradict רב.

steps.title: שמואל explains the משנה to fit רב: the channel runs past the pit
steps.stepSummary: שמואל himself explains the משנה in a way that works for רב: the channel runs right by the pit's opening, so the pit fills on its own without any damming.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל explained the משנה according to רב: it is talking about a channel that runs right past the mouth of the pit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge to רב, and the answer comes from שמואל, רב's own opponent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the channel flows right by the pit, water goes in without anyone blocking the river. That is the 'flows on its own' case from step 15, where everyone agrees. So the משנה is no proof for שמואל and no problem for רב.

keyTerms.meaning: At the mouth (opening) of his pit

phrases.english: Shmuel explained it according to Rav:
with a channel that runs past the mouth of his pit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the משנה to a specific case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה gives priority to whoever is closest even when damming is needed, like שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about water that flows into the pit by itself, where everyone agrees, so it does not contradict רב.

steps.title: If the water flows in by itself, why does the משנה need to say it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the pit fills on its own, it is obvious that it fills first. Why would the משנה teach that?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does it need to be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 17 by saying it makes the משנה teach something obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 already said that when water flows on its own, everyone agrees. If the משנה is only about that kind of case, it seems to add nothing. The גמרא expects a משנה to teach something new.

keyTerms.meaning: What is there to say? (It is obvious)

phrases.english: If so, what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's explanation in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the משנה is about a channel running past the pit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the pit fills by itself, its priority is obvious, so the משנה would be teaching nothing new.

steps.title: The new lesson: the others cannot force him to dam his pit and take a fair share
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is needed because we might have thought the other owners could tell him: 'Block your pit too, and water by a fair measure like us.' The משנה teaches that they cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that the others can tell him: 'Dam it up, and water by a fair measured share.' So the משנה teaches us that he does not have to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the משנה does teach something new, which ends this round of back-and-forth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even when the water flows in by itself, the neighbors might want equal sharing. They could demand that he block his pit and take only a measured portion like everyone else. The משנה rules that he may let his pit fill first, so the משנה is not obvious after all.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said: introduces a mistaken assumption
It teaches us (that the assumption is wrong)

steps.whatToRemember: רב: downstream fields water first; שמואל: upstream fields first. They argue only when the river must be dammed. The משנה about the pit fits רב because the channel flows right into the pit. It still teaches something: the owner cannot be forced to block his pit and take only a measured share.

phrases.english: You might have said, they can say to him:
phrases.notes: "They" are the other owners who share the channel.

phrases.english: Dam it up, and water by a fair measure;
phrases.notes: They are saying: block your pit from filling by itself, and take only your measured share like us.

phrases.english: It teaches us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the משנה teaches something new (מהו דתימא / קא משמע לן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The other owners could force the pit owner to block his pit and take only a measured share.
steps.terutzMaskana: The pit owner does not have to block his pit; it fills first.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה fits רב, and it teaches that a pit the channel flows into may fill first without being forced into equal shares.

steps.title: No decided הלכה: whoever is stronger wins
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר תחליפא rules that since the הלכה was never decided between רב and שמואל, the rule is כל דאלים גבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר תחליפא said: Since no one ever ruled like רב or like שמואל, whoever is stronger gets the water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the practical bottom line for the argument between רב and שמואל about upper and lower fields. Since nobody decided the הלכה, בית דין stays out, and whoever is stronger wins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two opinions were never decided either way, so בית דין cannot pick a winner. Instead the sides are left to settle it themselves. כל דאלים גבר does not mean violence is good. It is a way of handling a case the court cannot rule on.

keyTerms.meaning: Whoever is stronger prevails; the court does not step in
Neither like this master nor like that master

steps.whatToRemember: With no decided הלכה between רב and שמואל on river water, the rule is כל דאלים גבר.
steps.confusionAlert: כל דאלים גבר does not mean the stronger side is right. It means בית דין cannot decide, so it lets the parties settle it themselves.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the stage for the story right after it, where רב שימי בר אשי 'wins' the water by being clever while the others argue.

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Tachalifa said:
Now that the halacha was not stated
neither like this master nor like that master,
phrases.notes: The two 'masters' are רב and שמואל from before.

phrases.english: whoever is stronger prevails.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא דְּלָא אִיתְּמַר הִלְכְתָא לָא כְּמָר וְלָא כְּמָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical result of the רב/שמואל argument after the משנה was explained in a way that fits both.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Since the הלכה is undecided, בית דין does not rule, and whoever is stronger wins.

steps.title: A student offers to water אביי's fields so they can learn
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי asks אביי for a learning time. אביי is busy by day and must water his fields at night, so רב שימי offers to do the watering during the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר אשי asked אביי to set a time to learn with him. אביי said his time was already taken. 'Then at night?' אביי said he had to water his fields. רב שימי said, 'I'll water for you by day, and you learn with me at night.' אביי agreed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story that shows the rule of כל דאלים גבר in real life. This step is the setup: it explains why רב שימי בר אשי ended up watering אביי's fields.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's day was full of his own learning, and his nights went to watering. רב שימי solved the problem by taking over the watering. That sets up the next step, where we see how he got the water.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the master set (a time) for us

phrases.aramaic: רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּאַבָּיֵי,
phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ashi came before Abaye,
he said to him: Let the master set a time for me!

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִית לִי עִידָּנָא לְדִידִי.
phrases.english: He said to him: I have a time for myself.
Then let the master set a time for me at night!

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִית לִי מַיָּא לְאַשְׁקוֹיֵי.
phrases.english: He said to him: I have water to bring to irrigate.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא מַשְׁקֵינָא לֵיהּ לְמָר מַיָּא בִּימָמָא,
phrases.english: He said to him: I will irrigate for the master by day,
and let the master set a time for me at night!
He said to him: Very well.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּאַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a story that shows how כל דאלים גבר plays out in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup: רב שימי בר אשי takes on the job of watering אביי's fields.

steps.title: The clever watering and אביי's refusal to eat
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי tells each group the other side goes first. While they argue, he dams the river and waters אביי's fields. אביי objects and will not eat that year's produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went to the upper owners and said, 'The lower ones water first.' He went to the lower owners and said, 'The upper ones water first.' While they were busy, he dammed the river and watered. When he came to אביי, אביי said, 'You used two opposite opinions for me!' אביי did not eat that year's produce.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי gets the water by playing the two groups against each other while they argue. אביי is unhappy with how it was done and refuses to eat the produce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To the upper owners he quoted the view of רב (lower fields first), and to the lower owners the view of שמואל (upper fields first). That kept both groups busy so he could water in between. אביי objected that this used two opinions that contradict each other, and he did not even taste that year's fruit.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי would not benefit from water gained by playing both opinions against each other. He treated it as water that reached his field improperly.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a court's 'hands-off' rule is not a license for tricks. אביי saw water gained by telling each side a different, contradicting ruling as improperly obtained, so he would not benefit from it.

phrases.english: He went to the upper ones and said to them:
The lower ones drink the water first.
phrases.notes: This is רב's view, that the river flows its natural way down.

phrases.english: He went to the lower ones and said to them:
The upper ones drink the water first.
phrases.notes: Now he quotes שמואל's view, that the closer fields go first.

phrases.english: In the meantime, he dammed the river and irrigated.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּאַבָּיֵי, אֲמַר לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: When he came before Abaye, Abaye said to him:
You acted for me according to two opinions!
And Abaye did not taste
the produce of that year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: this is how רב שימי actually got the water.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי disapproved of gaining water by using both opinions against each other, and he did not eat that year's produce.

steps.title: The people of בי חרמך divert the river
steps.stepSummary: The residents of בי חרמך dug a channel from the head of the river שנוותא and returned the water lower down. The upper owners complained to אביי, who told them to dig a little deeper along with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some people from בי חרמך dug a channel at the head of the river שנוותא, sent the water around, and returned it at the end of the river. The upper owners came to אביי and said, 'They are damaging our river!' אביי told them, 'Dig a little deeper along with them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second story about water rights. A group changed the river's path, and the people above complained. אביי first offers a simple fix.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing the river's path changed how the water flowed to the other fields. אביי's first idea was not to stop בני בי חרמך. He suggested the others dig deeper so they would still get enough water.

keyTerms.meaning: The residents of a place called בי חרמך

phrases.english: There were certain residents of Bei Charmach
who went and dug at the head of the Shanvata,
phrases.notes: שנוותא is the name of the river.

phrases.english: and they returned it and released it at the end of the river.
The upper ones came before Abaye,
they said to him: It is damaging our river!

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: כְּרוֹ בַּהֲדַיְיהוּ טְפֵי פּוּרְתָּא.
phrases.english: He said to them: Dig a little deeper along with them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story about river water, this time about changing the river's path.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי's first approach: let the others fix the problem by digging deeper themselves.

steps.title: אביי orders the diverters to stop
steps.stepSummary: The upper owners reply that digging deeper would dry out their pits. אביי then tells the people of בי חרמך to remove themselves from there.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him, 'Then our pits will dry up.' He said to them, 'Go, remove yourselves from there.'
steps.whatsHappening: The complainers explain why אביי's fix will not work. אביי then gives a final ruling: the diverters must leave and stop changing the river.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the fix itself would cause real harm, digging deeper was no longer a solution. So אביי ruled against בני בי חרמך. They may not change the river's path in a way that harms others.
steps.whatToRemember: If changing a river's path causes harm that cannot be fixed, the people who changed it must stop.

phrases.english: They said to him: Our pits will dry up.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: זִילוּ סַלִּיקוּ נַפְשַׁיְיכוּ מֵהָתָם.
phrases.english: He said to them: Go, remove yourselves from there.
phrases.notes: He is now speaking to the people of בי חרמך, telling them to undo their channel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The upper owners reject אביי's first suggestion, and he gives a final ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אביי orders בני בי חרמך to stop diverting the river, since it harms the others.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about traps and starting to discuss two kinds of nets
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule about animals, birds and fish caught in a trap. Then it begins a comment about specific traps called אוזלי and אוהרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: "Traps for animals, birds and fish — taking from them counts as stealing, etc." The גמרא now comments: "With nets and woven traps..." (the sentence continues next).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה, about taking an animal out of someone else's trap. It names two kinds of traps, which sets up the comment that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this point the סוגיא was about water rights between neighbors. Now the topic changes to what is inside another person's trap. The משנה calls this stealing because of דרכי שלום, while רבי יוסי calls it full stealing. By naming אוזלי and אוהרי, the גמרא is getting ready to say how this rule works for these particular kinds of traps.

keyTerms.meaning: Traps or snares used to catch animals, birds or fish
"Etc." — a sign that only the start of a quote is given

steps.confusionAlert: The words בְּאוּזְלֵי וְאוֹהָרֵי are not a full sentence. They open the גמרא's comment, and the rest of the comment comes on the next עמוד.

phrases.english: Traps for animals, birds, and fish,
there is in them, etc.
phrases.notes: The full line says taking from them is stealing because of דרכי שלום, and רבי יוסי says it is full stealing.

phrases.english: With regard to nets and woven traps,

steps.triggerLanguage: מְצוּדוֹת חַיָּה וְעוֹפוֹת וְדָגִים, יֵשׁ בָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the stories about water channels (steps 21–24) and opens the next line of the משנה, about traps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Taking an animal, bird or fish from another person's trap is a kind of stealing. The גמרא now begins to apply this rule to nets and woven traps.
